identity.title: Gaia2: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Dynamic and Asynchronous Environments

problem.claim: Evaluate LLM agents in realistic asynchronous environments with temporal constraints, dynamic events, ambiguity, and multi-agent collaboration.

gap.claim: Prior evaluations are described as predominantly static or synchronous and do not capture these conditions.

contributions.claim: Introduces Gaia2 for evaluating LLM agents in dynamic, asynchronous environments.
Pairs each scenario with a write-action verifier for fine-grained action-level evaluation and potential reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards.
Releases Gaia2 with the open-source Agents Research Environments platform, using a consumer environment and an extensible design.

stated_novelty.claim: The benchmark combines independently evolving environments, temporal constraints, noisy dynamic events, ambiguity, collaboration, and write-action verification in one evaluation setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that no evaluated model dominates across capabilities; GPT-5 achieves the strongest overall score at 42% pass@1 but fails on time-sensitive tasks.
The authors report that Claude-4 Sonnet trades accuracy and speed for cost, while Kimi-K2 leads among open-source models at 21% pass@1.
The authors report trade-offs among reasoning, efficiency, and robustness, alongside challenges in closing the sim2real gap.

narrative_sequence.summary: Gaia2 targets realistic asynchronous agent evaluation beyond static or synchronous settings.
Scenario-specific write-action verifiers support fine-grained action-level assessment and verifiable-reward training.
Model comparisons show capability trade-offs rather than a single dominant system, with reported pass@1 figures and time-sensitive failures.
Gaia2 and the ARE framework are presented as extensible infrastructure for developing, benchmarking, and training practical agents.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links specific environment demands to a write-action verifier and then reports capability-specific model trade-offs.

lessons.interpretation: Aligning benchmark conditions, evaluation granularity, and reported outcomes can make aggregate scores less misleading.
lessons.application: For an agent benchmark, define scenario-level environmental demands and evaluate the concrete actions that satisfy them, then report per-capability failures alongside aggregate scores.
lessons.exception: This approach may be unsuitable when outcomes cannot be represented as verifiable writes or when interaction timing is irrelevant.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the number or composition of scenarios, verifier implementation, or evaluation protocol.
The reported model comparisons lack details on prompts, budgets, hardware, cost measurement, and statistical uncertainty.
The basis and evaluation procedure for the claimed sim2real challenges are not described.
